ledger.clause:
8.3 Properties listed for sale (§11.5)
STD-8.8 A property is considered listed for sale under §11.5 if it has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from (a) the last date of being listed to (b) the Application Date. \[G §11.5, p. 12\]

STD-8.9 Loans on such properties will be considered under the following characteristics: the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for investment properties, the subject must be occupied by a tenant and may not be vacant; the loan must qualify as either (a) ≥ 1.0 DSCR or (b) 43% maximum DTI (Q-14); a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is required unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves are required, and cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; the loan must have a fully amortizing term, interest only is not available; the maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of (a) appraised value or (b) lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is allowed; impounds are required. \[G §11.5, pp. 11–12\]

STD-8.9 Loans on such properties will be considered under the following characteristics: the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for investment properties, the subject must be occupied by a tenant and may not be vacant; the loan must qualify as either (a) ≥ 1.0 DSCR or (b) 43% maximum DTI (Q-14); a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is required unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves are required, and cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; the loan must have a fully amortizing term, interest only is not available; the maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of (a) appraised value or (b) lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is allowed; impounds are required. \[G §11.5, pp. 11–12\]

STD-8.5 A vacant property may be purchased; qualifying rents are taken from the 1007 or 1025 (STD-3.8). “Vacant investment properties are only eligible for a refinance transaction if consistent with §10.17.” \[G §5.32, p. 3; §3.41, p. 11\]

STD-8.6 Rate and term refinance of a vacant property (§10.17): minimum 700 FICO score; maximum \$1,000,000 to maximum 70% CLTV; maximum \$2,000,000 to maximum 65% CLTV; minimum 1.000 DSCR or maximum 40.0% DTI (Q-14); minimum two-year prepayment penalty (where allowable); full amortization required, no interest-only programs; impounds required; minimum six months reserves. The Summary states the same conditions with “Max CLTV 70% for loan amounts under \$1,000,000 and 65% for loan amounts under \$2,000,000”. Treatment at exactly \$1,000,000 and \$2,000,000: Acra confirmation requested → Q-10. \[G §10.17, p. 11; S: Occupancy Type\]

STD-8.7 Cash-out refinance of a vacant property: the “Cash-Out Refinances” heading in §10.17 is empty in the excerpt. The Summary states: minimum 700 FICO; DSCR ≥ 1.15; ≥ 3-year PPP (where allowable); no interest only; impounds required; 6 months reserves; “Max CLTV 60% for loan amounts under \$1,500,000”; “Requires ≥15 months ownership”. Loans of \$1,500,000 or more, and how the 15 months are measured: Acra confirmation requested → Q-10. \[S: Occupancy Type; G §10.17, p. 11\]

ledger.clause:
1.2 Loan amount, contributions and gifts
STD-1.10 Minimum loan amount \$100,000; maximum loan amount \$3,000,000; loan amount to be in \$50 increments. \[S: Loan Amount\]

STD-1.11 Seller concession / other contributions: limited to 3% of the sale price. \[S: Loan Amount\]

STD-1.12 Gifting is allowed and “requires borrower to contribute a minimum of 10% of the purchase price consisting of their own funds”; §8.7 states the contribution as the applicant's “own sourced and seasoned funds”. Gift documentation requirements are in the Seller's Guide gift-fund section, not reproduced (Appendix B). \[S: Loan Amount; G §8.7, p. 12\]

9.1 Gift funds, funds to close and seasoning
STD-9.1 Gift funds, investment property or second homes: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price. Gift documentation requirements are in the Seller's Guide gift-fund section (Appendix B). \[G §8.7, p. 12; S: Loan Amount\]

STD-9.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing and Foreign Nationals, regardless of LTV / CLTV, need to document a minimum of 60 days seasoning.” Whether the repatriation requirement applies to any borrower holding funds abroad or only to foreign nationals, and what evidence applies: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

ledger.clause:
9.2 Reserves by trigger, as stated
STD-9.6 The sources state reserves only for the situations below, and state the payment basis only where shown. The base requirement where no trigger applies, the payment basis where only “months” is stated, permitted sources, whether overlapping triggers are cumulative, and whether reserves substituted for rent loss insurance are additional: Acra confirmation requested → Q-07. \[S; G\]

| **Trigger** | **Reserves as printed** | **Source** |
|----|----|----|
| LTV \> 80.00% | 6 months PITIA reserves | S: Income Documentation |
| FICO \< 620 | 12 Months | S: Credit Requirements |
| First-time homebuyer | Minimum six months reserves (“Requires 6mos Reserves”) | G §3.13; S: Restrictions |
| Vacant property — rate & term refinance | Minimum six months reserves | G §10.17; S: Occupancy Type |
| Vacant property — cash-out refinance | 6 months reserves | S: Occupancy Type |
| Property listed for sale within six months | Twenty-four (24) months of reserves; cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide | G §11.5 |
| Forbearance or mortgage lates in the last 12 months, tenant-occupied subject, without timely receipt of the prior two months' rent | 12 months of the subject's payment in reserve, which may be from the transaction's cash-in-hand | G §5.32 |
| Rent loss insurance required but cannot be obtained | Two (2) months reserves for every one (1) month of coverage not provided | G §23.40 |

condition.purpose: Determine whether the stated 12 months of the subject's payment in reserve requirement is met for the specified trigger.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the loan application, rent documentation, and reserve documentation.
Eligibility Verification: Determine whether there is forbearance or mortgage lates in the last 12 months, the subject is tenant-occupied, and the prior two months' rent was not received timely.
Validation and Verification: Where all trigger conditions apply, verify 12 months of the subject's payment in reserve; the reserve may be from the transaction's cash-in-hand.
Final Determination: Determine whether the stated reserve requirement is met.
checks: The full trigger does not apply, or reserves equal at least 12 months of the subject's payment.
If used, transaction cash-in-hand is included as reserve.

outcomes.criterion: The full trigger does not apply, or there are 12 months of the subject's payment in reserve, which may be from the transaction's cash-in-hand.
The trigger facts, subject's payment amount, or reserves remain to be established.
The full trigger applies and reserves are less than 12 months of the subject's payment.
There is no case for this outcome.

9.1 Gift funds, funds to close and seasoning
STD-9.1 Gift funds, investment property or second homes: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price. Gift documentation requirements are in the Seller's Guide gift-fund section (Appendix B). \[G §8.7, p. 12; S: Loan Amount\]

STD-9.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

STD-9.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing and Foreign Nationals, regardless of LTV / CLTV, need to document a minimum of 60 days seasoning.” Whether the repatriation requirement applies to any borrower holding funds abroad or only to foreign nationals, and what evidence applies: Acra confirmation requested → Q-12. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

condition.purpose: Verify that the entity borrower has provided the required entity documentation without exception.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the entity documents for the required formation documents and amendments; operating agreement or bylaws and amendments; ownership evidence; applicable stock certificates, ledger, affidavit, K-1 statements, and CPA or Tax Preparer letter; name matching or a letter of explanation; good-standing certificate; applicable foreign qualification; EIN documentation; and unanimous written consent or board resolution.

Eligibility Verification: Confirm that the submitted documents include the requirements applicable to the entity type and transaction; do not accept a borrower letter stating that required documents are not required, available, or excused.

Validation and Verification: Verify that the documents are complete and legible, contain the specified authorization, management, signer, and ownership information, and that the Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent is valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.
Final Determination: Record whether all applicable required documents have been provided and verified; refer any additional supporting-documentation condition imposed by Legal for clearance.
checks: All applicable required entity documents are provided, complete, legible, and meet the stated content requirements; no borrower letter is accepted in place of a required document.
The Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document is valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

ledger.clause:
6.2 Entity documentation
STD-6.10 The documents below are required, without exception, and borrower letters stating that they are not required, available, or excused from providing such documents are not acceptable. \[G §3.12, pp. 8–9\]

- Complete, legible copy of the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments thereto.

- Complete (with all referenced exhibits), legible copy of the Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, and all amendments, that states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Additional information may be required if the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict.

- All documentation evidencing ownership interests: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement must identify, or attach as an exhibit, all persons by name with their ownership interest, or provide copies of the membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement.

- For S or C Corporations: shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation's stock ledger. The certificate or ledger must account for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is required.

- For S-corporations or Partnerships, where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable: (i) the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest, and (ii) a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.

6.2 Entity documentation
- Names on the entity documents must match the identification; if they do not match exactly, a letter of explanation is required to address the discrepancy.

- Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

- Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted, if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.

- IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity. EIN exception requests may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

- A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, (i) authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and (ii) identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. It may be required by the Operating Agreement or Bylaws even where ownership is held by one individual. It cannot be used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee, only an authorized signor for the loan documents signed by the entity.

- A Power of Attorney must be utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee; see §23.5(C), not reproduced (Appendix B).

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

condition.purpose: Determine whether an entity borrower meets the stated entity-form, formation, and SPE eligibility requirements.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the loan application and entity documents to identify the borrower, the entity’s formation and location, its entity type, its purpose, and the assets and activities described for it.

Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the transaction is a business purpose transaction for an investment property exclusively; whether the entity is a US formed and based Entity; whether its type is allowed; and whether it is a single purpose entity as defined in the guideline.
Validation and Verification: Verify from the entity documents that the entity is not a series LLC, an excluded entity type, or an impermissible nested ownership structure.
Final Determination: Record whether the entity borrower meets the stated eligibility requirements.
checks: The entity borrower’s transaction is a business purpose transaction for an investment property exclusively.
The entity borrower is a US formed and based Entity of an allowed type.

The entity borrower is a single purpose entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties and is engaged in owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.

The entity borrower is not a series LLC, a Cooperative, an Irrevocable Trust, a Land Trust, an IRA, a Non-Profit, or a Joint Venture, and its ownership structure does not exceed the stated nesting limit.

ledger.clause:
6.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
STD-6.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

6.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
STD-6.8 Not allowed: Cooperatives, Irrevocable Trusts, Land Trusts, IRAs, Non-Profit, and Joint Ventures. “Business entity nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary that in turn must be owned by individual(s); multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera are not acceptable.” An illustration of the permitted structure: Acra confirmation requested → Q-22. \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

STD-6.9 Acra requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience. At least one (1) borrower / guarantor on the loan must attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer; if prior home ownership is not evident within the loan file, the underwriter reserves the right to condition for supporting documentation. See Q-09. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

Appendix A — Acra confirmation register
“Business entity nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary that in turn must be owned by individual(s)”. | Please confirm the permitted structure with an example — for instance, whether the borrowing entity may be wholly owned by one holding entity that is itself owned by individuals. |  |
| Q-23 Source versions (section 1.4). Summary 6.15.2026 V1.1 (supplied) versus 8.17.2026 (published); Guidelines August 28, 2026. | Which Summary version governs, and are both sources the controlling versions for this program? |  |
| Q-24 Prepayment terms and “BUY-OUT” (STD-11.2, 11.3). State rows read “BUY-OUT all Residential 1-4” and similar; vacant-property and listed-for-sale minimums apply “where allowable”. | \(a\) What does “BUY-OUT” require — no prepayment penalty on that loan, or a priced alternative? (b) Where a state restriction removes the penalty, are the vacant-property and listed-for-sale minimum terms waived? |  |
| Q-25 Sections referred to but not supplied (Appendix B). | Please supply them, or confirm that none changes a requirement in this document. |  |
| Q-26 DSCR denominator on interest-only loans (STD-3.2, 10.6). §7.5: “Acra calculates the DSCR utilizing the first payment due under the terms of the Note”; Interest Only payments are “the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest … on a monthly basis”; §5.32 denominator: “annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and … association fees”. | On an interest-only loan, is the DSCR computed on the interest-only payment plus taxes, insurance and association fees, or on the fully amortized payment? |  |
| Q-27 Business-purpose scope (STD-1.3, 9.2). The Summary is listed as “Business Purpose DSCR”; §5.32 requires the attestation “under a business purpose transaction”; §8.4 refers to “consumer transactions”. | Is every loan on this program a business-purpose transaction, or can a DSCR loan be a consumer transaction, and if so with what differences? |  |

6. Borrowing entities, guarantors and trusts (§3.12)
Section 3.12 governs loans to entities, the personal guarantees Acra requires, the entity documentation it accepts and title vesting in a revocable living trust. It is restated here as requirements; nothing in it is program-specific.

condition.purpose: Determine whether the entity borrower’s required guarantor arrangements meet the stated requirements.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the loan application and entity documents for direct and indirect ownership interests, recourse guarantors, and any homeownership attestation.
Eligibility Verification: Identify every individual with direct or indirect ownership of at least 20% and determine whether at least one guarantor has prior homeownership experience.

Validation and Verification: Verify that each individual with direct or indirect ownership of at least 20% provides an Acra approved recourse guarantee or Exhibit 7, and that recourse is joint and several when there are multiple guarantors.
Final Determination: Record whether the required guarantors and guarantees are established; identify any supporting documentation for prior homeownership that the underwriter conditions for.
checks: All individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% provide an Acra approved recourse guarantee or Exhibit 7.
Recourse is joint and several when there are multiple guarantors.
At least one guarantor has prior homeownership experience.
At least one borrower / guarantor on the loan attests on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer.

outcomes.criterion: Every step is met and every check holds.
Prior homeownership is not evident within the loan file and the underwriter conditions for supporting documentation; the condition must be cleared.
A step is not met or a check does not hold.
The borrower is not an entity borrower.

missing_reads: Direct and indirect ownership percentages; identities of guarantors; guarantee documents and whether they are Acra approved or Exhibit 7.
Evidence of prior homeownership where it is not evident within the loan file; any supporting documentation conditioned for by the underwriter.

rule.description: Verify required recourse guarantees and the stated homeownership-experience requirement for entity borrowers.

ledger.clause:
6.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
STD-6.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

STD-6.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

6.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
STD-6.8 Not allowed: Cooperatives, Irrevocable Trusts, Land Trusts, IRAs, Non-Profit, and Joint Ventures. “Business entity nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary that in turn must be owned by individual(s); multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera are not acceptable.” An illustration of the permitted structure: Acra confirmation requested → Q-22. \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

STD-6.9 Acra requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience. At least one (1) borrower / guarantor on the loan must attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer; if prior home ownership is not evident within the loan file, the underwriter reserves the right to condition for supporting documentation. See Q-09. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether relevant changes to an entity’s operating agreement or bylaws are recognized for required-guarantor purposes.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the entity’s operating agreement or bylaws and amendments, and identify changes intended to change ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors.
Eligibility Verification: Compare the date of each identified change with the Application Date and the application process period.
Validation and Verification: Determine whether any identified change occurred within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process.
Final Determination: Do not recognize any change that falls within the stated period when determining required personal guarantors.
checks: No change to the operating agreement or bylaws intended to change ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors occurred within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process.

outcomes.criterion: Every step is met and every check holds.
There is no case for this outcome.
A step is not met or a check does not hold.
The borrower is not an entity borrower, or no relevant change to the operating agreement or bylaws is identified.

missing_reads: Operating agreement or bylaws amendments, the intent of each ownership-percentage change, the Application Date, and the dates covering the application process.

rule.description: Check whether ownership-percentage changes intended to circumvent required personal guarantors fall within the stated non-recognition period.

condition.purpose: Determine whether title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust meets the stated requirements.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the complete, legible trust or the Certification of Trust, and the title commitment for trust vesting.

Eligibility Verification: Verify that the trust is valid under the laws of the state in which it is established, revocable, established by one or more natural persons during their lifetime, and has the individual(s) establishing the trust as its primary beneficiary.

Validation and Verification: Verify the required trust information and provisions, including trustee powers, authority to hold title and mortgage the property, beneficiary consent or written consent, absence of unusual risk or impairment to lender rights, and that trust vesting does not diminish lender rights as a creditor. Verify that written exception by Acra Senior Management is obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.
Final Determination: Record whether each applicable trust-vesting requirement is met and whether any additional supporting-documentation condition imposed by Legal has been cleared.
checks: A complete, legible copy of the Trust or a Certification of Trust containing all information specified in the guideline is provided.

The trust is valid under the laws of the state in which it is established, revocable, established by one or more natural persons during their lifetime, and has the individual(s) establishing it as its primary beneficiary.
The trust provides the specified trustee powers, beneficiary consent provision, absence-of-risk provision, and protection of the lender’s rights as a creditor.
Written exception by Acra Senior Management is obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.
Any additional supporting documentation conditioned for by Legal is provided.

outcomes.criterion: Every step is met and every check holds, and any Legal condition for additional supporting documentation has been cleared.
Legal conditions for additional supporting documentation; the condition must be cleared.
A step is not met or a check does not hold.
Title is not vested in an inter vivos revocable trust.

ledger.clause:
6.4 Revocable living trusts
STD-6.13 Title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust is permitted when all of the following requirements are followed. \[G §3.12, pp. 9–10\]

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust, or a Certification of Trust stating: the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and the current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of the Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and a statement that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

- The Trust must be valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.

- The Trust must be revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime. Irrevocable trust is not permitted.

- The Trust must be established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and must become effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.

- The primary beneficiary of the Trust must be the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

- Written exception by Acra Senior Management must be obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.

- The Trust must specify that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

7.2 Mortgage / rental rating and payment history
STD-7.6 The mortgage / rental rating for determining mortgage pricing is determined by evaluating the ratings for properties the borrower owns and / or rents over the last twelve (12) months. All reported mortgages on credit should be considered; where the applicant has mortgages that are not reported, the file should contain documentation to evaluate history on the applicant's primary residence(s), any secondary residence(s), and the subject property. \[G §4.15, p. 5\]

STD-7.7 DSCR loans only require documentation on the subject property, principal residence, and second home (if any) of the borrower and / or guarantor(s). Additional properties do not require housing history to be documented unless documents in the file suggest a major credit event has occurred, for example a foreclosure listing the borrower (individually or as guarantor) on the credit report. For DSCR loans, the payment history is required for the primary residence, subject property, and second homes, if applicable. \[G §4.15, p. 5; §6.7, p. 6\]

STD-7.8 Loans that have matured are rated based on the maturity date of the loan; any extensions of the maturity date must be in writing. \[G §4.15, p. 5\]

condition.purpose: Verify documentation of mortgage and rental history used for mortgage pricing and, for DSCR loans, the specified property payment history.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the credit report and available file documentation for mortgages, rental history, and properties owned and/or rented over the last twelve (12) months.

Eligibility Verification: Establish whether the loan is a DSCR loan and identify the subject property, principal residence, second home (if any), reported mortgages, and any major credit event indicated by file documents.

Validation and Verification: For mortgage pricing, evaluate the ratings for properties the borrower owns and/or rents over the last twelve (12) months. Consider all reported mortgages on credit; where mortgages are not reported, review documentation for the applicant’s primary residence(s), any secondary residence(s), and the subject property. For DSCR loans, verify documentation and payment history for the subject property, principal residence, and second home (if any) of the borrower and/or guarantor(s); do not require housing history documentation for additional properties unless documents in the file suggest a major credit event has occurred.
Final Determination: Record whether the required housing-history documentation and payment history are documented for the applicable scope.

Eligibility Verification: Establish whether an event applies and select the Purchase or Refi R/T, Refi C/O column.

Validation and Verification: Compare seasoning and CLTV with the printed rows: ≥ 24 Mo—No Restrictions; 12-23 Mo—80% Purchase, 75% Refi R/T, Refi C/O; < 12 Mo—75%, 70%. Record separately that the printed text says “FB Taken ≤6 Mos: Case-by-case”; its meaning and timing require Acra confirmation.
Final Determination: Record whether the applicable printed restriction is met and whether clarification is outstanding for “FB Taken ≤6 Mos: Case-by-case” when relevant.
checks: If a short sale, deed-in-lieu or modification applies, CLTV does not exceed the printed maximum for its seasoning row and loan-purpose column.
If “FB Taken ≤6 Mos” is relevant, its meaning and timing have been confirmed by Acra.

outcomes.criterion: The applicable event restriction is met and, if relevant, Acra has confirmed the meaning and timing of “FB Taken ≤6 Mos: Case-by-case”.
Acra confirmation of the meaning and timing of “FB Taken ≤6 Mos: Case-by-case” remains outstanding when relevant.
CLTV exceeds the applicable printed maximum.
No short sale, deed-in-lieu or modification applies, and “FB Taken ≤6 Mos” is not relevant.

missing_reads: Acra confirmation of the meaning and timing of “FB Taken ≤6 Mos: Case-by-case,” if relevant.

condition.purpose: Determine the borrower’s citizenship type for applying the identification requirements.

Step 4 - Final Determination: Record the borrower’s citizenship type.

ledger.clause:
4.1 Citizenship types and limits
STD-4.1 Eligible borrower citizenship types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident, Non-Permanent Resident, Foreign National, ITIN. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.2 Permanent Resident must have an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.3 Non-Permanent Resident must have proof of legal residency, which may include an unexpired employment authorization document (EAD) or valid visa. Limit printed as “Max Loan Amount: \$1.5M: Max CLTV 80%” — whether this is two independent limits or one conditional limit: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.4 Foreign National: “Borrowers whose Primary Residence is not located in the United States of America.” Maximum CLTV 70% (purchase) and 65% (refinance — rate & term and cash-out); “Price loan at FICO equal to 700”. No maximum loan amount is stated for foreign nationals: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. Program documentation is in section 5. \[S: Borrower Citizenship\]

STD-4.5 ITIN: “ITIN is defined as any non-resident that is unable to provide any of the ‘Non-Permanent Resident Alien’ documents listed above.” Maximum loan amount \$1.0M; minimum FICO 640; maximum CLTV by FICO as printed below. §3.10 separately admits ITIN holders under the foreign-national program when they reside outside the US. Whether a US-resident ITIN holder is eligible, and whether the tier printed “FICO 700” means 700 and above: Acra confirmation requested → Q-03. \[S: Borrower Citizenship; G §3.10, p. 6\]

| **ITIN tier as printed** | **Purchase** | **Refinance — R/T and cash-out** |
|--------------------------|--------------|----------------------------------|
| “FICO 700”               | 70%          | 65%                              |
| “FICO 660 to 699”        | 65%          | 60%                              |
| “FICO 640 to 659”        | 60%          | 60%                              |

condition.purpose: Determine whether the required account documentation and seasoning evidence are provided.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the two (2) most recent statements of the account holding the funds.
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the funds have been seasoned for a minimum of sixty (60) days.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: If funds are not seasoned a minimum of sixty (60) days, verify a letter of explanation and information to comprise a sixty (60) day chain of funds. Verify that bank statements in any language other than English are translated into English.
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the account statements and applicable seasoning, explanation, chain-of-funds, and translation documentation meet the requirement.
checks: The two (2) most recent account statements are provided, and funds are seasoned a minimum of sixty (60) days or, if not, a letter of explanation and information to comprise a sixty (60) day chain of funds are provided; bank statements in any language other than English are translated into English.

outcomes.criterion: The required two (2) most recent statements are provided, the seasoning requirement is met or the specified alternative documentation is provided, and any bank statements in a language other than English are translated into English.

5.2 Assets held in foreign accounts
STD-5.6 Assets held / foreign accounts must be verified in U.S. Dollar equivalency at the current exchange rate via www.xe.com or the Wall Street Journal conversion table. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.7 Sufficient funds to close must be on deposit with the Escrow / Closing Agent at least three (3) business days (including Saturdays for this calculation) prior to any closing date. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.8 A copy of the two (2) most recent statements of that account is required. If the funds are not seasoned a minimum of sixty (60) days, a letter of explanation is required along with the information to comprise a sixty (60) day chain of funds. Bank statements in any language other than English must be translated into English. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.9 Per §8.4, Foreign Nationals, regardless of LTV / CLTV, need to document a minimum of 60 days seasoning, and funds held in a foreign bank / currency must be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing (STD-9.5). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

5.4 Closing documents
STD-5.11 Each of the following must be met: a copy of current Passport, Visa, or ITIN; all loans closed with a title and closing agent approved and / or vetted by Acra; Power of Attorney acceptable provided it conforms to Acra requirements and is acceptable to the title company; executed W-8 (BEN) IRS form. \[G §3.10, p. 7\]

STD-5.12 Documents signed outside of the U.S. may be notarized by a U.S. embassy or consular official; the certificate of acknowledgement must include the embassy or consular seal and be acceptable to the title company. For documents signed in a country that is party to the Hague Convention Treaty Abolishing the Requirement of Legalization for Foreign Public Documents, a certificate of acknowledgment completed and signed by an authorized notary public plus authentication by apostille in English, attached to the executed documents, with title company acceptance, is agreeable to Acra. \[G §3.10, p. 7\]

ledger.clause:
5.1 Eligibility
STD-5.1 Foreign Nationals are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions only (i.e. investment properties). \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.2 Eligible under the Foreign National Program are Non-Resident Aliens who are not authorized to live or work in the U.S. “A true Foreign National may periodically visit the U.S. for various reasons including vacation and / or business, may purchase property for limited personal use or investment, or may own a U.S based business entity, but they must reside outside of the U.S.” \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.3 Borrowers who are holders of Individual Tax Identification Numbers (ITIN) are eligible for this program if they reside outside of the U.S. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.4 “Due to market exchange rates, applicants are to be reviewed with scrutiny toward a post-close financial position and their ability to mitigate exchange rate fluctuations.” \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.5 “See 3.10 for OFAC restrictions and state specific exclusions” — not reproduced (Appendix B). \[G §3.10, p. 7\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether documents signed outside the U.S. meet one of the described notarization routes and title company acceptance requirement.
steps: Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Identify closing documents signed outside of the U.S. and review their acknowledgment and authentication materials.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the documents were notarized by a U.S. embassy or consular official, or signed in a country that is party to the Hague Convention Treaty Abolishing the Requirement of Legalization for Foreign Public Documents.

5. Foreign national program (§3.10)
Section 3.10 of the Seller's Guide, reproduced in the excerpt, governs foreign nationals on business-purpose transactions. Its OFAC restrictions and state-specific exclusions are referred to but not reproduced.

5.1 Eligibility
STD-5.1 Foreign Nationals are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions only (i.e. investment properties). \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.2 Eligible under the Foreign National Program are Non-Resident Aliens who are not authorized to live or work in the U.S. “A true Foreign National may periodically visit the U.S. for various reasons including vacation and / or business, may purchase property for limited personal use or investment, or may own a U.S based business entity, but they must reside outside of the U.S.” \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.3 Borrowers who are holders of Individual Tax Identification Numbers (ITIN) are eligible for this program if they reside outside of the U.S. \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.4 “Due to market exchange rates, applicants are to be reviewed with scrutiny toward a post-close financial position and their ability to mitigate exchange rate fluctuations.” \[G §3.10, p. 6\]

STD-5.5 “See 3.10 for OFAC restrictions and state specific exclusions” — not reproduced (Appendix B). \[G §3.10, p. 7\]

STD-5.11 Each of the following must be met: a copy of current Passport, Visa, or ITIN; all loans closed with a title and closing agent approved and / or vetted by Acra; Power of Attorney acceptable provided it conforms to Acra requirements and is acceptable to the title company; executed W-8 (BEN) IRS form. \[G §3.10, p. 7\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the loan meets the stated DSCR-below-1.0 or No Ratio CLTV and FICO limits.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the case's DSCR qualification information, loan purpose, CLTV, and credit score.
Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the loan has DSCR below 1.0 or is No Ratio, and identify purchase, rate & term refinance, or cash-out refinance purpose.
Validation and Verification: Verify CLTV does not exceed 75% for purchase, 70% for refinance—rate & term, or 65% for refinance—cash-out, and verify minimum FICO 640.
Final Determination: Record whether the applicable limits are met.
checks: For DSCR below 1.0 or No Ratio, CLTV does not exceed 75% for purchase, 70% for refinance—rate & term, or 65% for refinance—cash-out.
For DSCR below 1.0 or No Ratio, FICO is at least 640.

ledger.clause:
3.4 Ratio-dependent conditions
STD-3.16 LTV \> 80.00%: requires a minimum DSCR of 1.20 and 6 months PITIA reserves; limited to SFR, Warrantable Condos outside of Florida, Townhome, PUD. Stated in LTV where the matrix is labelled CLTV: Acra confirmation requested → Q-17. \[S: Income Documentation\]

STD-3.17 DSCR \< 1.0 or No Ratio: maximum CLTV 75% (purchase), 70% (refinance — rate & term), 65% (refinance — cash-out); minimum FICO 640. \[S: Income Documentation\]

STD-3.18 “The minimum rental income required is outlined in the Program Matrix.” The minimum ratios stated for particular situations across both sources are collected below; each is also stated in its own section. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

| **Situation** | **Minimum DSCR as stated** | **Source** |
|----|----|----|
| LTV above 80.00% | 1.20 | S: Income Documentation |
| Loan amount over \$2,000,000 | 1.0 | S: Loan Amount |
| 1 or no score / deficient tradelines | 1.1 | S: Credit Requirements |
| Rural / unique property | 1.00 | S: Subject Property Location |
| Non-warrantable condo; condotel / PUDtel | 1.0 | S: Subject Property Type |
| First-time homebuyer | 1.150 | G §3.13; S: Restrictions |
| Vacant property, rate & term refinance | 1.000 (“OR Maximum 40.0% DTI” — Q-14) | G §10.17; S: Occupancy Type |
| Vacant property, cash-out refinance | 1.15 | S: Occupancy Type |
| Property listed for sale within six months | 1.0 (“or (b) 43% maximum DTI” — Q-14) | G §11.5 |
| Mixed use, adult care or assisted living | 1.2 | G §10.7 |

3.3 Rent schedules and rent evidence
STD-3.9 Acra requires the Single-Family Comparable Rent Schedule (FNMA Form 1007) for single family properties on (i) all DSCR qualifying files, (ii) lease-option purchase transactions where the down payment required in §3.45 is generated from excess monthly rent contributions, or (iii) when proposed rental income is being used to qualify. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.10 A 1007 may be from the original appraiser or any state licensed appraiser. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.11 Single family investment properties with excessive monthly rent payments reflected on the lease require documentation supporting that the monthly rent is typical for the area; acceptable documentation may include classified ads from local newspapers, a 1007 completed by the appraiser, or a market rent survey completed by a local real estate company or rental management company familiar with the market rents in the area. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.12 Short-term rental, appraisal form: for properties occupied as a short-term rental, an STRpro or similar appraisal form is acceptable as replacement to a 1007 as long as it is signed by an appropriately licensed appraiser. \[G §14.13, p. 4\]

STD-3.13 Short-term rental, actual rents: “Acra can accept short term rentals with 12-month ledgers from condotel management companies, property managers, AirBnB, VRBO, etcetera as documentation for actual rents.” How a 12-month ledger establishes qualifying rent, and how the receipt and lease conditions of STD-3.6 apply to short-term rentals: Acra confirmation requested → Q-02. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §14.13, p. 4\]

STD-3.14 Short-term rental caps: “Properties qualifying with short-term rentals are limited to 75% & 70% LTV / CLTV for Purchase or Refinance transactions respectively”; the Summary states maximum CLTV 75% (purchase) and 70% (refinance — rate & term and cash-out), minimum FICO 640. \[G §5.32, p. 3; S: Occupancy Type\]

ledger.clause:
3.1 The ratio
STD-3.1 “Acra calculates the DSCR by dividing (a) the lesser of (i) annual in-place rent or (ii) market rent (reference §14.14) by (b) the sum of annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees (collectively, ‘PITIA’). Subordinate financing, if applicable, would also be included in the denominator for the sake of this calculation.” \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.2 “Acra calculates the DSCR utilizing the first payment due under the terms of the Note.” §7.5 defines Interest Only payments as “the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest to the mortgage on a monthly basis at the time of origination”, while the §5.32 denominator lists “annual principal, interest …”. Which payment enters the DSCR denominator on an interest-only loan: Acra confirmation requested → Q-26. \[G §7.5, p. 13; §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.3 The reference to subordinate financing in the denominator is a calculation rule; it does not itself establish that a subordinate lien is permitted. Whether and when subordinate financing is permitted: Acra confirmation requested → Q-18. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

STD-3.4 §14.14 (market rent), referenced in the formula, is not reproduced in the excerpt (Appendix B). \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

3.3 Rent schedules and rent evidence
STD-3.9 Acra requires the Single-Family Comparable Rent Schedule (FNMA Form 1007) for single family properties on (i) all DSCR qualifying files, (ii) lease-option purchase transactions where the down payment required in §3.45 is generated from excess monthly rent contributions, or (iii) when proposed rental income is being used to qualify. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.10 A 1007 may be from the original appraiser or any state licensed appraiser. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.11 Single family investment properties with excessive monthly rent payments reflected on the lease require documentation supporting that the monthly rent is typical for the area; acceptable documentation may include classified ads from local newspapers, a 1007 completed by the appraiser, or a market rent survey completed by a local real estate company or rental management company familiar with the market rents in the area. \[G §14.12, p. 4\]

STD-3.12 Short-term rental, appraisal form: for properties occupied as a short-term rental, an STRpro or similar appraisal form is acceptable as replacement to a 1007 as long as it is signed by an appropriately licensed appraiser. \[G §14.13, p. 4\]

STD-3.13 Short-term rental, actual rents: “Acra can accept short term rentals with 12-month ledgers from condotel management companies, property managers, AirBnB, VRBO, etcetera as documentation for actual rents.” How a 12-month ledger establishes qualifying rent, and how the receipt and lease conditions of STD-3.6 apply to short-term rentals: Acra confirmation requested → Q-02. \[G §5.32, p. 3; §14.13, p. 4\]

STD-3.14 Short-term rental caps: “Properties qualifying with short-term rentals are limited to 75% & 70% LTV / CLTV for Purchase or Refinance transactions respectively”; the Summary states maximum CLTV 75% (purchase) and 70% (refinance — rate & term and cash-out), minimum FICO 640. \[G §5.32, p. 3; S: Occupancy Type\]

ledger.clause:
1.1 Occupancy, purpose and qualification
STD-1.1 Occupancy is investment property (non-owner occupied) only. \[S: Occupancy Type\]

STD-1.2 An investment property is “a one- to four-unit residential dwelling or a unit in a condominium complex or a PUD owned by an individual who does not occupy the dwelling. The dwelling is leased and occupied as a principal year-round residence to individuals other than the owner.” \[G §3.41, p. 11\]

STD-1.3 The Program Summary is listed as “Business Purpose DSCR” on Acra's rate-sheet page. “Where the borrower is qualifying utilizing the subject property's actual or market cashflow under a business purpose transaction, borrower must execute with loan docs a Business Purpose Attestation (Exhibit 8) or other similar attestation approved by Acra.” The excerpt's §8.4 also refers to consumer transactions (STD-9.2); whether every loan on this program is a business-purpose transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-27. \[G §5.32, p. 3; acralending.com/ratesheets\]

STD-1.4 The matrix columns are Purchase, Rate & Term and Cash-Out. Delayed financing is addressed only by the matrix footnote “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM”. Which column and which cash-in-hand rule apply to delayed financing: Acra confirmation requested → Q-06. \[S: matrix and footnote\]

STD-1.5 A loan qualifies either by a calculated DSCR (§5.32) or as No Ratio DSCR, where no ratio is calculated (§5.33). Both are set out in section 3. \[G §5.32–5.33, p. 3\]

STD-1.6 “Borrowing entity income documentation not required.” Acra will not calculate a DTI for applicants who qualify using a DSCR; income or employment listed on an application is superfluous to the underwrite and may be left blank, and if represented, a DTI should not be calculated. \[S: Income Documentation; G §7.3, p. 5\]

ledger.clause:
7.3 Properties listed for sale (§11.5)
PLAT-7.6 A property is considered listed for sale under §11.5 if it has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from (a) the last date of being listed to (b) the Application Date. \[G §11.5, p. 12\]

PLAT-7.7 Whether §11.5 applies to Platinum Select unchanged is part of Q-13; it is restated here because the Platinum Summary does not exclude it. \[G §11.5\]

PLAT-7.8 Loans on such properties will be considered under the following characteristics: the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for investment properties, the subject must be occupied by a tenant and may not be vacant; the loan must qualify as either (a) ≥ 1.0 DSCR or (b) 43% maximum DTI — on this program the channel minimum DSCR applies, Wholesale 1.0 and Correspondent 1.2 (PLAT-3.8), and the DTI alternative is Q-14; a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is required unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves are required, and cash-in-hand may be considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; the loan must have a fully amortizing term, interest only is not available; the maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of (a) appraised value or (b) lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is allowed; impounds are required. \[G §11.5, pp. 11–12\]

ledger.clause:
8.1 Gift funds, funds to close and seasoning
PLAT-8.1 Gift funds, investment property: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price (PLAT-1.15). \[G §8.7, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction is Q-22. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing”. Foreign nationals are not eligible for this program, but an eligible US citizen or permanent resident may hold funds abroad; the same sentence's 60-day seasoning requirement is stated for Foreign Nationals only and is not restated. Whether the repatriation requirement applies to eligible borrowers holding funds abroad, and what evidence and timing convention apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.6 “See guidelines for unacceptable source of funds” — the Seller's Guide provision is not reproduced (Appendix B). \[P: Reserve Requirements\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether applicant(s) contribute the required minimum portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to an investment property transaction.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the loan application and bank statement(s) for information about the transaction, purchase price, and applicant funds.
Eligibility Verification: Determine from the transaction documentation whether this is an investment property transaction.

Validation and Verification: Verify from the documentation that applicant(s) contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction that is at least 10% of the purchase price.
Final Determination: Record whether the required minimum contribution is verified.
checks: For an investment property transaction, applicant(s) contribute at least 10% of the purchase price in their own sourced and seasoned funds.

outcomes.criterion: The transaction is an investment property and the required minimum contribution of applicant(s)’ own sourced and seasoned funds is verified.
There is no case for this outcome.
The transaction is an investment property and applicant(s) do not contribute the required minimum of their own sourced and seasoned funds.
The transaction is not an investment property.

condition.purpose: Determine whether funds-to-close seasoning is verified when the stated consumer or business-purpose transaction trigger applies.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the bank statement(s) or VOD reflecting funds to close and the recent account information.

Validation and Verification: If the applicable trigger is met, verify seasoning of funds to close from the account documentation. Do not apply a domestic-funds seasoning period beyond the 30-days documentation minimum on the basis of this provision.

8.1 Gift funds, funds to close and seasoning
PLAT-8.1 Gift funds, investment property: applicant(s) are required to contribute a portion of their own sourced and seasoned funds to the transaction at a minimum of 10% of the purchase price (PLAT-1.15). \[G §8.7, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.2 Verification of the seasoning of funds to close is required on loans over 70% CLTV for consumer transactions, or business purpose loans where funds to close are over \$50,000 and over 70% CLTV. Whether any loan on this program is a consumer transaction is Q-22. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.3 Where the account(s) serving as the source of funds must be verified, verification may include a copy of the borrower's bank statement(s) for the most recent month(s), or a VOD reflecting a current and average balance for the most recent month(s). \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.4 “All transactions require a minimum of 30-days documentation.” Whether any seasoning period applies to domestic funds beyond this documentation minimum: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.5 “In contrast to the above, but consistent with §3.10.1 of this Guide, funds held in a foreign bank / currency will need to be repatriated at minimum three (3) business days prior to Closing”. Foreign nationals are not eligible for this program, but an eligible US citizen or permanent resident may hold funds abroad; the same sentence's 60-day seasoning requirement is stated for Foreign Nationals only and is not restated. Whether the repatriation requirement applies to eligible borrowers holding funds abroad, and what evidence and timing convention apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-11. \[G §8.4, p. 12\]

PLAT-8.6 “See guidelines for unacceptable source of funds” — the Seller's Guide provision is not reproduced (Appendix B). \[P: Reserve Requirements\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the borrower entity has an allowed form and ownership structure.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the loan_application and entity_documents for the entity's type, formation, ownership, and any subsidiary structure.
Eligibility Verification: Confirm the entity is one of the allowed types; is US formed and based; is not a foreign owned entity; and does not have a prohibited form or ownership structure.

ledger.clause:
5.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
PLAT-5.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

5.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
PLAT-5.8 Not allowed: Cooperatives, Irrevocable Trusts, Land Trusts, IRAs, Non-Profit, and Joint Ventures. “Business entity nesting is limited to only one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary that in turn must be owned by individual(s); multiple nesting or ownership by multiple entities, trusts, etcetera are not acceptable.” An illustration of the permitted structure: Acra confirmation requested → Q-18. \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

PLAT-5.9 Acra requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience. At least one (1) borrower / guarantor on the loan must attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer; if prior home ownership is not evident within the loan file, the underwriter reserves the right to condition for supporting documentation. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the entity documentation required without exception is provided and satisfies the specified requirements.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review entity_documents for the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and amendments; applicable Operating Agreement or Bylaws and amendments; ownership-interest evidence; required certificates, ledger, affidavit, K-1 statements and CPA or Tax Preparer letter where applicable; good standing; foreign qualification where applicable; EIN documentation; unanimous written consent / board resolution; and any applicable power of attorney.

Eligibility Verification: Confirm that the package contains the documents applicable to the entity type and transaction. Borrower letters stating that required documents are not required, available, or excused from providing them are not acceptable.

Validation and Verification: Verify legibility, completeness, required contents and signatures; name matching or a letter of explanation; Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent validity within ninety (90) days of the closing date; and any applicable Legal review or additional supporting-documentation condition.
Final Determination: Record whether the required documentation is complete, or identify a permitted outstanding condition or unmet requirement.
checks: The required entity documents are provided without exception and satisfy the stated content, legibility, name, validity, ownership-evidence, and applicable qualification requirements; borrower letters excusing required documents are not accepted.

outcomes.criterion: All applicable required entity documents are provided and satisfy the stated requirements.
Legal requires additional supporting documentation, or an applicable EIN exception request or other expressly stated review or approval remains to be resolved.
A required document or requirement is unmet, including where a borrower letter is offered in place of a required document.
The borrower is not an entity borrower.

missing_reads: The applicable entity-document types and contents, entity names and identification match, ownership evidence, entity management and borrowing authority, designated signers, certificates and ledger details, any lost-stock affidavit, any K-1 statements and CPA or Tax Preparer letter, good-standing validity relative to closing, qualification requirements, EIN documentation, unanimous written consent / board resolution, and any required power of attorney or additional supporting documents.

rule.description: Review the entity-document package for every required document, content, validity period, and stated exception process.

- Complete (with all referenced exhibits), legible copy of the Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, and all amendments, that states whether the entity is member or manager managed, contains authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designates signers. Additional information may be required if the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict.

- All documentation evidencing ownership interests: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement must identify, or attach as an exhibit, all persons by name with their ownership interest, or provide copies of the membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement.

- For S or C Corporations: shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or, if stock certificates are lost or unavailable, the corporation's stock ledger. The certificate or ledger must account for all outstanding shares noted in the Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate is required.

- For S-corporations or Partnerships, where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable: (i) the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest, and (ii) a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.

5.2 Entity documentation
- Names on the entity documents must match the identification; if they do not match exactly, a letter of explanation is required to address the discrepancy.

- Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent document valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date.

- Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted, if the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located.

- IRS Form SS4 or Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity. EIN exception requests may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds.

- A Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, (i) authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and (ii) identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. It may be required by the Operating Agreement or Bylaws even where ownership is held by one individual. It cannot be used to designate a signor on a personal guarantee, only an authorized signor for the loan documents signed by the entity.

- A Power of Attorney must be utilized by the principal to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee; see §23.5(C), not reproduced (Appendix B).

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

5.4 Revocable living trusts
PLAT-5.13 Title vesting in an inter vivos revocable trust is permitted when all of the following requirements are followed. \[G §3.12, pp. 9–10\]

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust, or a Certification of Trust stating: the existence and date of the Trust; the Trustor(s) and the current Trustee(s); the powers of the Trustee; whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; the names and number of the Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; the Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to the Trust assets should be taken; and a statement that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

- The Trust must be valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.

- The Trust must be revocable, meaning it can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime. Irrevocable trust is not permitted.

- The Trust must be established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly (Grantor, Trustor, or Settlor), and must become effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.

- The primary beneficiary of the Trust must be the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

- Written exception by Acra Senior Management must be obtained if the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same.

- The Trust must specify that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property; that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

- Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

5.1 Entity eligibility and guarantees
PLAT-5.1 Business Entities are eligible for financing on business purpose transactions (investment properties exclusively). \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.2 Acra will lend to, and require that title to the collateral be held, either (i) directly by an individual person(s) or (ii) by an entity acceptable to Acra in its sole discretion. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.3 Acra requires all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% to provide a recourse guarantee (Acra approved, or Exhibit 7) in the case of an entity borrower. All recourse is joint and several in the case of multiple guarantors. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.4 An entity borrower must be a single purpose entity (SPE): “an entity with no assets other than residential investment or rental properties; engaged in the business of owning and operating residential investment or rental properties.” Series limited liability companies are not allowed. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.5 All entities that will hold direct ownership of the subject property and will be on title as a direct owner are required to be a borrowing entity. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.6 Changes to the operating agreement or bylaws with the intent of changing ownership percentages to circumvent required personal guarantors will not be considered. “Lookback to changes cannot occur within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process as these changes will not be recognized by Acra Lending.” \[G §3.12, p. 7\]

PLAT-5.7 Entity / guarantor types allowed: Domestic Corporations (C and S Corp); single purpose Limited Liability Companies (LLC), excluding series LLC; Limited Liability Partnership (LLP); Limited Liability Limited Partnership (LLLP); General Partnership (GP); Limited Partnership (LP); and Sole Proprietorship. “In all events, the Borrower must be a US formed and based Entity, foreign entities (i.e.: entities formed or based outside the US) or foreign owned entities are not allowed.” \[G §3.12, p. 8\]

ledger.clause:
6.1 Decisioning score and tradelines
PLAT-6.1 “Decisioning Credit Score: Primary Wage Earner middle score. For loans that close in the name of an entity, use the highest middle score of the personal guarantors, presuming equal percentages of ownership. If ownership percentages differ, use the individual with the highest concentration of ownership.” \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.2 Minimum decisioning score 700 (no matrix row below 700, PLAT-2.1); Correspondent pricing limited to 60% CLTV for 700-719 (PLAT-2.3). \[P: matrix; footnote 3\]

PLAT-6.3 “Tradelines: Applicants with scores from 3 repositories are deemed to be acceptable with no tradeline overlay. 2 tradelines & 24 month history or 3 tradelines & 12 month history for applicants with 2 or fewer scores.” \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.4 Applicants with one score are within “2 or fewer scores” for the tradeline requirement above. The Platinum Summary does not state how the decisioning score is set with one score or with two scores, whether any no-score pathway exists, or how “Primary Wage Earner” is identified on a file with no income documentation. The Standard Summary's one-or-no-score provision is not restated here: Acra confirmation requested → Q-05. \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.5 Where two or more guarantors hold an equal largest ownership interest and ownership is not equal across all guarantors, PLAT-6.1 does not say whose score is used: Acra confirmation requested → Q-05. \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

condition.purpose: Determine the decisioning credit score under PLAT-6.1.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the credit report and application for the primary wage earner’s middle score; for an entity borrower, review each personal guarantor’s middle score and ownership percentage.

Eligibility Verification: For a non-entity loan, identify the Primary Wage Earner’s middle score. For a loan closing in an entity’s name, use the highest middle score of the personal guarantors when ownership percentages are equal; if ownership percentages differ, use the individual with the highest concentration of ownership.
Validation and Verification: Verify the score and, where applicable, ownership information against the reviewed documents.
Final Determination: Record the score selected under PLAT-6.1. If the file does not establish the necessary person or score, do not infer one.

For loans that close in the name of an entity, use the highest middle score of the personal guarantors, presuming equal percentages of ownership. If ownership percentages differ, use the individual with the highest concentration of ownership.” \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.2 Minimum decisioning score 700 (no matrix row below 700, PLAT-2.1); Correspondent pricing limited to 60% CLTV for 700-719 (PLAT-2.3). \[P: matrix; footnote 3\]

PLAT-6.3 “Tradelines: Applicants with scores from 3 repositories are deemed to be acceptable with no tradeline overlay. 2 tradelines & 24 month history or 3 tradelines & 12 month history for applicants with 2 or fewer scores.” \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.4 Applicants with one score are within “2 or fewer scores” for the tradeline requirement above. The Platinum Summary does not state how the decisioning score is set with one score or with two scores, whether any no-score pathway exists, or how “Primary Wage Earner” is identified on a file with no income documentation. The Standard Summary's one-or-no-score provision is not restated here: Acra confirmation requested → Q-05. \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

PLAT-6.5 Where two or more guarantors hold an equal largest ownership interest and ownership is not equal across all guarantors, PLAT-6.1 does not say whose score is used: Acra confirmation requested → Q-05. \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements\]

ledger.clause:
4. Borrower eligibility
The Platinum Summary lists two eligible citizenship types and excludes first-time homebuyers. Borrowing entities, guarantors and trusts follow the Seller's Guide excerpt and are in section 5.

PLAT-4.1 Eligible borrower citizenship types: US Citizen, Permanent Resident. \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.2 Permanent Resident must have an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89. \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.3 Non-permanent residents, foreign nationals and ITIN borrowers are not among the listed eligible types. The Seller's Guide foreign-national program (§3.10) is therefore not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Borrower Citizenship Requirements\]

PLAT-4.4 “First Time Homebuyer (FTHB) ineligible for this program”. Acra defines a First Time Home Buyer as “an application where all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property)”; the §3.13 DSCR allowance for first-time homebuyers is not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Borrower Credit History Requirements; G §3.13, p. 10\]

PLAT-4.5 §3.12 requires at least one guarantor to have prior homeownership experience, and at least one borrower / guarantor to attest on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer (PLAT-5.9). Whether it applies to individual borrowers as well as entities is part of Q-13. \[G §3.12, p. 7\]
