condition.purpose: Verify the requirement for a 1007 on DSCR transactions and the single-family rent-schedule requirement.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the file for a Single-Family Comparable Rent Schedule (FNMA Form 1007).
Eligibility Verification: Confirm that the case is a DSCR transaction; for a single-family property, apply the single-family requirement for all DSCR qualifying files.
Validation and Verification: Verify that Form 1007 is present. Do not treat a Form 1025 alone as satisfying the requirement for a two-unit property; that question is unresolved in the source.

3.1 Qualifying rent, as printed in the Platinum Summary
PLAT-3.1 “When calculating the DSCR, Acra will use the greater of the market rent as established on the 1007 or 1025, or actual rent. When using actual rent, the actual rent must be documented via evidence of 2 months’ proof of receipts and the lease must be in place for at least 3 months after the loan closing. This applies to long-term rents only and is not appropriate for short-term rentals.” \[P: Income Documentation & Debt Ratio Requirements\]

PLAT-3.2 §5.32 of the excerpt states the general formula as “the lesser of (i) annual in-place rent or (ii) market rent”, then notes that “Acra may use the higher of actual or market rents” subject to “two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt”, a lease continuing at least three months after closing, and: “Security Deposit does not count towards receipt, and the rents cannot be prepaid.” The Platinum Summary's statement (PLAT-3.1) is program-specific; the excerpt's general formula is reproduced here. Which governs Platinum Select and how they relate, whether “2 months’ proof of receipts” means consecutive months, and whether the security-deposit and prepaid-rent conditions apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-03. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.3 Short-term rentals are ineligible for the program (PLAT-7.2); the Seller's Guide provisions on short-term rental income and appraisal forms are not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Subject Property Requirements\]

ledger.clause:
3.2 The ratio
PLAT-3.4 Denominator, per §5.32: “the sum of annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees (collectively, ‘PITIA’). Subordinate financing, if applicable, would also be included in the denominator for the sake of this calculation.” \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.5 “Acra calculates the DSCR utilizing the first payment due under the terms of the Note.” §7.5 defines Interest Only payments as “the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest to the mortgage on a monthly basis at the time of origination”, while the §5.32 denominator lists “annual principal, interest …”. Which payment enters the DSCR denominator on an interest-only loan: Acra confirmation requested → Q-21. \[G §7.5, p. 13; §5.32, p. 3\]

The Platinum Summary does not address subordinate financing or restate the Standard Summary's HELOC calculation: Acra confirmation requested → Q-15. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

ledger.clause:
3.1 Qualifying rent, as printed in the Platinum Summary
PLAT-3.1 “When calculating the DSCR, Acra will use the greater of the market rent as established on the 1007 or 1025, or actual rent. When using actual rent, the actual rent must be documented via evidence of 2 months’ proof of receipts and the lease must be in place for at least 3 months after the loan closing. This applies to long-term rents only and is not appropriate for short-term rentals.” \[P: Income Documentation & Debt Ratio Requirements\]

PLAT-3.2 §5.32 of the excerpt states the general formula as “the lesser of (i) annual in-place rent or (ii) market rent”, then notes that “Acra may use the higher of actual or market rents” subject to “two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt”, a lease continuing at least three months after closing, and: “Security Deposit does not count towards receipt, and the rents cannot be prepaid.” The Platinum Summary's statement (PLAT-3.1) is program-specific; the excerpt's general formula is reproduced here. Which governs Platinum Select and how they relate, whether “2 months’ proof of receipts” means consecutive months, and whether the security-deposit and prepaid-rent conditions apply: Acra confirmation requested → Q-03. \[G §5.32, p. 3\]

PLAT-3.3 Short-term rentals are ineligible for the program (PLAT-7.2); the Seller's Guide provisions on short-term rental income and appraisal forms are not restated (Appendix B). \[P: Subject Property Requirements\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether required rent loss insurance is provided for six (6) months or the stated reserve substitution is met when the coverage cannot be obtained.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review hazard insurance declarations for the rent loss coverage period provided; review available loan information for reserves.
Eligibility Verification: Confirm that the rent loss insurance requirement applies, using the Rent Loss Insurance Applicability determination.

Validation and Verification: If the requirement applies, verify that six (6) months' rent loss insurance is provided. When required rent loss insurance cannot be obtained, assess whether reserves provide two (2) months for every one (1) month of rent loss coverage not provided.
Final Determination: Record whether the required coverage or permitted reserve substitution is met; identify any outstanding condition or unmet requirement.
checks: If rent loss insurance is required and cannot be obtained, reserves are at least two (2) months for every one (1) month of the six (6) months' rent loss coverage not provided; otherwise, six (6) months' rent loss insurance is provided.

outcomes.criterion: The rent loss insurance requirement applies and six (6) months' rent loss insurance is provided, or required rent loss insurance cannot be obtained and the permitted reserve substitution is met.
The rent loss insurance requirement applies, required coverage cannot be obtained, and the permitted reserve substitution remains to be cleared.
The rent loss insurance requirement applies and neither six (6) months' rent loss insurance nor the permitted reserve substitution is met.
The Rent Loss Insurance Applicability determination establishes that rent loss insurance is not required.

7.4 Rent loss insurance (§23.40)
PLAT-7.9 Rent loss insurance covers rental losses that are incurred during the period that a property is being rehabilitated following a casualty. \[G §23.40, p. 13\]

PLAT-7.10 Six (6) months' rent loss insurance is required on one- to four-unit non-owner occupied income properties with LTV \> 70% and when subject property rents are used to qualify. \[G §23.40, p. 13\]

PLAT-7.11 “Loans with ≤ 70% CLTV are not required to carry rent loss insurance.” The requirement is stated in LTV and the exemption in CLTV; the case of LTV at or below 70% with CLTV above 70%: Acra confirmation requested → Q-10. \[G §23.40, p. 13\]

PLAT-7.12 When rent loss insurance is required but cannot be obtained, the borrower may substitute two (2) months reserves for every one (1) month of rent loss coverage not provided. \[G §23.40, p. 13\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the subject property and loan meet the stated conditions for required rent loss insurance, including the CLTV exemption and the stated LTV/CLTV discrepancy.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the loan application and rent roll for the subject property's income-property status and whether subject property rents are used to qualify; review available loan information for LTV.

Eligibility Verification: Establish whether the subject property is one- to four-unit, non-owner occupied, and an income property; establish whether subject property rents are used to qualify and whether LTV is greater than 70%.

Validation and Verification: Check CLTV against the stated exemption: loans with ≤ 70% CLTV are not required to carry rent loss insurance. If LTV is at or below 70% and CLTV is above 70%, request Acra confirmation.
Final Determination: Record whether the rent loss insurance requirement applies, does not apply, or is pending the stated Acra confirmation.

The subject property is non-owner occupied.
The subject property is an income property.
The subject property's LTV is greater than 70%.
Subject property rents are used to qualify.
The loan's CLTV is greater than 70%.

1.1 Occupancy, purpose and qualification
PLAT-1.1 Occupancy: Non-Owner Occupied. \[P: Occupancy Requirements\]

PLAT-1.2 An investment property is “a one- to four-unit residential dwelling or a unit in a condominium complex or a PUD owned by an individual who does not occupy the dwelling. PLAT-1.3 The Program Summary is listed as “Business Purpose DSCR Platinum” on Acra's rate-sheet page. “Where the borrower is qualifying utilizing the subject property's actual or market cashflow under a business purpose transaction, borrower must execute with loan docs a Business Purpose Attestation (Exhibit 8) or other similar attestation approved by Acra.” The excerpt's §8.4 also refers to consumer transactions (PLAT-8.2); whether every loan on this program is a business-purpose transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-22. \[G §5.32, p. 3; acralending.com/ratesheets\]

PLAT-1.4 Eligible loan purpose types: Purchase, Rate & Term Refinance, Cash-Out Refinance, Delayed Financing. The matrix footnote states “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM”; which matrix column and which cash-in-hand rule apply to delayed financing: Acra confirmation requested → Q-02. \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements; matrix footnote\]

PLAT-1.5 “Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) Cash-Out Refinance Transactions requires current lease agreement”. \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements\]

PLAT-1.6 “Vacant properties ineligible”. The Seller's Guide provisions on vacant purchases and §10.17 vacant refinances therefore do not apply (Appendix B). \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements\]

1.1 Occupancy, purpose and qualification
PLAT-1.1 Occupancy: Non-Owner Occupied. \[P: Occupancy Requirements\]

PLAT-1.2 An investment property is “a one- to four-unit residential dwelling or a unit in a condominium complex or a PUD owned by an individual who does not occupy the dwelling. The dwelling is leased and occupied as a principal year-round residence to individuals other than the owner.” The property types the Platinum Summary lists as eligible are at PLAT-7.1; types it does not list are set out in the table at 7.1 and asked in Q-07. \[G §3.41, p. 11; P: Subject Property Requirements\]

PLAT-1.3 The Program Summary is listed as “Business Purpose DSCR Platinum” on Acra's rate-sheet page. “Where the borrower is qualifying utilizing the subject property's actual or market cashflow under a business purpose transaction, borrower must execute with loan docs a Business Purpose Attestation (Exhibit 8) or other similar attestation approved by Acra.” The excerpt's §8.4 also refers to consumer transactions (PLAT-8.2); whether every loan on this program is a business-purpose transaction: Acra confirmation requested → Q-22. \[G §5.32, p. 3; acralending.com/ratesheets\]

PLAT-1.4 Eligible loan purpose types: Purchase, Rate & Term Refinance, Cash-Out Refinance, Delayed Financing. The matrix footnote states “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM”; which matrix column and which cash-in-hand rule apply to delayed financing: Acra confirmation requested → Q-02. \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements; matrix footnote\]

PLAT-1.5 “Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR) Cash-Out Refinance Transactions requires current lease agreement”. \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements\]

PLAT-1.6 “Vacant properties ineligible”. The Seller's Guide provisions on vacant purchases and §10.17 vacant refinances therefore do not apply (Appendix B). \[P: Loan Purpose Requirements\]

11.3 Published differences from the Standard program
| **Topic** | **Standard Summary** | **Platinum Select Summary** |
|----|----|----|
| Minimum FICO (matrix) | 600 | 700 |
| Maximum loan amount | \$3,000,000 | \$2,000,000 |
| Best-case CLTV (purchase / rate & term / cash-out) | 85% / 80% / 80% | 80% / 80% / 75% |
| Loan-size caps | \< \$200,000: 80% / 75% | \< \$350,000 or \> \$1,500,000: 75.00% |
| Channel rules | None stated | Correspondent DSCR ≥ 1.2; Correspondent 700-719 limited to 60% CLTV |
| Qualifying rent | Per Seller's Guide §5.32 (lesser-of formula with higher-of note) | “Greater of the market rent … or actual rent” |
| Minimum DSCR | 1.20 above 80% LTV; below 1.0 and No Ratio permitted with caps | 1.0 Wholesale; 1.2 Correspondent |
| Citizenship | US Citizen, Permanent Resident, Non-Permanent Resident, Foreign National, ITIN | US Citizen, Permanent Resident |
| First-time homebuyer | Allowed with conditions | Ineligible |
| Short-term rental | Allowed at 75% / 70%, FICO 640 | Ineligible |
| Vacant property | Purchase allowed; refinance under §10.17 | Ineligible |
| Cash-out refinance | No lease condition stated | Current lease agreement required |
| Property types | SFR, Townhome, PUD, Warrantable and Non-Warrantable Condo, Condotel / PUDtel, 2-4 Units, Manufactured | SFR, Townhome, PUD, Warrantable Condo, Two-Units |
| Rural property | Allowed with conditions | Ineligible |
| Ineligible locations | SD | SD, U.S. Terrs. |
| Mortgage history | Tiered caps to 0x90x12; 0x120x12 ineligible | 0x30x12 |
| Previous credit events | Bankruptcy / foreclosure: tiered caps, ineligible under 12 months; short sale / DIL / modification: tiered caps including under 12 months | 48 Mo Seasoning |
| Decisioning score | Not stated | Primary Wage Earner middle score; entity rule |
| Escrow waiver | \$1.5M; 80% CLTV; FICO 700; 0x30x24; no Foreign Nationals | \$1.5M; 0x30x24; Section 35 loans ineligible |
| Reserves (Summary triggers) | 6 months PITIA above 80% LTV;

9.2 Interest-only
PLAT-9.3 “Interest-Only (5 Yr Term), Max CLTV: 75.00%”. \[P: Product Requirements — Restrictions\]

PLAT-9.4 No minimum loan amount or minimum FICO is printed for interest-only loans on Platinum Select: Acra confirmation requested → Q-09. \[P: Product Requirements\]

PLAT-9.6 Interest Only payments are calculated as the amount sufficient to pay the accrued interest on the mortgage monthly at the time of origination, usually for a set term at the beginning of the repayment term; after that term the payments are recast to a fully amortized payment for the balance of the term ending at maturity. Acra calculates the DSCR using the first payment due under the Note (PLAT-3.5; which payment enters the denominator on an interest-only loan is Q-21). The excerpt's DTI calculation for interest-only loans is a DTI-program provision — Q-14. \[G §7.5, p. 13\]

condition.purpose: Determine whether the representative score and CLTV meet the printed Platinum Select matrix requirements.
steps: Initial Document Review: Review the credit_report and loan_application for the decisioning score, loan purpose, and CLTV.

Eligibility Verification: Apply the printed rows: at 730 and above, maximum CLTV is 80% Purchase / 80% Rate & Term / 75% Cash-Out; at 721 to below 730, 80% / 80% / 65%; at 700 to below 721, 80% / 80% / 55%. No row is printed below 700.
Validation and Verification: Verify the score, purpose, and CLTV against the case record and reviewed documents. Read the printed 721 threshold literally; do not normalize it to 720.
Final Determination: Determine whether the score is in a printed row and the CLTV does not exceed that row's limit for the loan purpose.
checks: The decisioning score is at least 700.
The loan CLTV does not exceed the printed matrix limit for the decisioning score and loan purpose.

outcomes.criterion: The decisioning score is at least 700, the applicable printed matrix row is used, the CLTV does not exceed that row's limit for the loan purpose, and every check holds.
There is no case for this outcome.
The decisioning score is below 700, no printed matrix row applies, the CLTV exceeds the applicable printed matrix limit, or a check does not hold.
There is no case for this outcome.

Appendix A — Acra confirmation register
Each item below is a point the two sources leave open or state in two ways. Acra's wording is quoted beside each question. This document adopts no reading of its own; where a requirement depends on an item, it is marked “Acra confirmation requested”. Please answer in the right-hand column, or attach the governing Seller's Guide provision.

Appendix A — Acra confirmation register
| **Question and Acra's source language** | **Confirmation requested** | **Acra response or correction** |
|----|----|----|
| Q-01 The 721 threshold and Correspondent limits (PLAT-2.1 to 2.3). Matrix rows: 730 / 721 / 700; footnote 3: “Correspondent Pricing limited to 60% CLTV for 700-719 FICO”; ARM margin bands 720-759 and 700-719. | \(a\) Is the 721 threshold intended, or should it read 720? (b) For a score of exactly 720: which matrix row, is it subject to the Correspondent 60% limit, and which ARM margin? (c) For Correspondent loans at 700-719, does the 60% limit apply to purchase and rate & term while the matrix's 55% governs cash-out? |  |
| Q-02 Delayed financing (PLAT-1.4, 2.4). Listed as an eligible loan purpose; footnote: “Delayed financing is capped at \$1.5MM”. | Which matrix column governs delayed financing, and which cash-in-hand rule applies? |  |
| Q-03 Qualifying rent (PLAT-3.1, 3.2). Platinum: “the greater of the market rent as established on the 1007 or 1025, or actual rent … 2 months’ proof of receipts … lease … in place for at least 3 months after the loan closing”. §5.32: “the lesser of …”; “two (2) consecutive months”; “Security Deposit does not count towards receipt, and the rents cannot be prepaid.” | \(a\) Does the Platinum greater-of rule govern this program in place of the §5.32 formula? (b) Must the 2 months of receipts be consecutive? (c) Do the security-deposit and prepaid-rent conditions apply? (d) Is any additional approval required to use actual rent? |  |
| Q-04 Rent form for two units (PLAT-1.10). §5.32: “A 1007 will always be required”; Platinum: market rent “as established on the 1007 or 1025”. | Does a Form 1025 alone satisfy the rent-schedule requirement for an eligible two-unit property? |  |
| Q-05 Credit score selection (PLAT-6.1, 6.4, 6.5). “Decisioning Credit Score: Primary Wage Earner middle score …”; tradelines for “applicants with 2 or fewer scores”.
